issues.evidence: All recorded facts match the sources and the claim is otherwise in order: reported 2026-10-14, within the 5-day deadline of Article 4.1; coverage C2 is in the Policy Schedule (Article 2); all C2 required documents are provided (Article 4.3); no Article 3 exclusion applies; deductible €0 is correct under the Article 5.2 not-at-fault waiver (not at fault and third party identified); no assessor needed since €1,200 is not above €1,500 (Article 6.1). HOWEVER, the handler playbook states: 'When the other driver is a commercial vehicle (van, truck, lorry, delivery vehicle), refer the claim to a handler so Veridia can recover the money from their insurer.' The accident report shows Vehicle B is a Ford Transit Custom, vehicle type 'Van', owned by Rapid Livraisons SARL (a delivery company) — a commercial delivery van. This playbook rule is triggered by facts stated in the documents, so the claim must be referred to a handler and must NOT be paid automatically; the staged automatic payout of €1,200 (status pending_approval) is therefore a concern.

verdict.summary: Every recorded fact matches the email, the signed accident report and the repair quote, and the claim meets the deadline, coverage, documents and deductible rules — but because the other vehicle is a commercial delivery van (Ford Transit Custom of Rapid Livraisons SARL, per the accident report), the playbook requires referral to a handler, so the staged €1,200 payment must not be approved automatically.
